title: Every htmx endpoint declared in markup has a test

facts.note: Templates/source files in the scan mount carrying hx-get/hx-post/hx-put/hx-patch/hx-delete attributes; every such declaration counts, whether or not it was changed.
The same scan mount must contain at least one test file; otherwise the rule is a no-op.

values: htmx_tester_detector: endpoint not mentioned by any test in the same mount
facts.note: Produced by the source-named validator htmx_tester_detector, which scans the whole mount (not a diff).

fires: A template gains hx-get="/x/y" and no test file in the same mount mentions /x/y.
An existing, unchanged template in a mount that contains tests declares an hx-post endpoint that no test file mentions.
A mount with tests has an hx-delete endpoint with a dynamic segment and no test hits any concrete path under its static prefix.
doesNotFire: The scan mount contains markup but no test files at all (coverage no-op).
A test hits a concrete id (e.g. /orders/1) for a templated endpoint /orders/:id.
The hx- endpoint is an absolute URL (that is coder.htmx.verb-endpoint-same-origin's finding).

given: A scan mount containing test files and markup declaring endpoints via htmx verb attributes (hx-get, hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch, hx-delete)
when: The mount is scanned: every declared hx- verb endpoint, changed or not, is checked against the mount's tests
then: Every endpoint declared by an htmx verb attribute MUST be exercised by at least one test in the same mount.
prefer:
Write a test exercising the endpoint: `
` (declared) is covered by `const res = await fetch("/invoices/overdue"); expect(res.status).toBe(200);` (exercised).
If the surface is not real, delete the hx- attribute instead.
Read the markup as the route space: the hx- attribute IS the request.
avoid: Adding an hx- verb attribute with no test, so a new server surface exists that nothing records.
Reporting endpoints uncovered on a source-only mount.
unless: The mount contains no test files: skip it entirely.
A dynamic segment matches on its static prefix (`/orders/1` covers `/orders/:id`).
why: An htmx endpoint is an element attribute, not an enumerable router-table entry, so the route space grows and is forgotten easily; this rule notices new surfaces. A coverage claim needs a suite to measure against, so without tests it stays silent.
evidence: htmx_tester_detector reports no endpoint that no test file in the same mount mentions.
For each hx- verb endpoint in the mount (changed or not), a test file in the same mount references it literally or up to a dynamic segment.
verifier_detail: Collect every hx- verb endpoint (hx-get, hx-post, hx-put, hx-patch, hx-delete) from templates and source; collect the text of every test file in the same mount; report an endpoint no test mentions.
Matching: a literal match counts, as does a match up to a dynamic segment (static-prefix match), so `/orders/1` covers `/orders/:id`.

Coverage no-op (term coverage_no_op): when a scan mount holds markup but no test files, emit nothing rather than report every endpoint uncovered. A coverage rule needs both sides; a source-only scan is not evidence of a missing test; and a tester-persona rule must not produce findings on a tree containing no tests. The no-op matters as much as the check.

Route space (term route_space): the set of endpoints the application actually exposes; for htmx it is every hx- verb attribute in the templates, because that attribute IS the request (for Convex it is the interlocking YAML). Reading markup rather than a plan file is not a boundary violation but the honest location of the declaration in this stack.
Skip absolute-URL endpoints; they belong to coder.htmx.verb-endpoint-same-origin.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Bun/htmx realization mirroring tester.convex.interlocking-route-coverage; the declaration source differs and that difference IS the adaptation — a Convex route is declared in plan/_trains/_interlockings/**/*.yaml, an htmx endpoint is declared in the markup, so the markup is this stack's route space. Direct counterpart of the Convex coverage rule; 'this is the rule that notices'.
